```markdown # DESIGN.md: The Bayes Group marketing site (prerendered static) > **Scope of the current change:** documentation only. `DEPLOYMENT.md` is updated so that it matches the seven-page site described below. No UI, copy, token, component or route changes. Every screen, state and acceptance test stays exactly as specified here. ## Users and goal **Users:** owners, operations leaders and technical managers at small and medium-sized businesses (first), plus enterprise leaders buying a premium program. They arrive from referrals, search or shared links, often on a phone, and they distrust AI hype. **The one job:** see within a minute that this is a senior engineering firm that builds specific, observable, sustainable AI systems at the right size for them, then book a consultation. **Success feels like:** "They have built this before, they will show me how it runs, and my team will own it." Shared links show real titles. Pages render complete with no flash. The message sends and is confirmed. ## Primary flow 1. Land on Home (`/`). The prerendered hero shows the h1, the value proposition, **Book a consultation** and **See how we build**. 2. Press **Book a consultation** (hero, header, Menu panel, every CTA band) to go to `/contact`. The page scrolls to the top and focus moves to `
`. 3. Fill in **Name**, **Email** and **Message**. **Company**, **Company size** and **What can we help with?** are optional. 4. Press **Send message**. The banner reads "Thanks, we'll be in touch within one business day." and the form clears. **Secondary paths** - **See how we build** → `/systems` → **Book a consultation**. - Who we serve → **See engagements** / **Enterprise engagements** → `/engagements` → a tier button → `/contact`. The header holds all six links and the CTA on every page. The footer's Services and Company columns also reach every page, so no page is a dead end. ## Screens and states The site is static: no data loading, no network, no spinners. React hydrates the prerendered HTML. Long words and the email use `overflow-wrap:anywhere`. Photos reserve their space with width/height (no layout shift). If an image fails to load, its alt text shows on the navy fallback background `#0B1F3A`. **Pages and built files** (what `npm run build` writes; `DEPLOYMENT.md` lists exactly these) | Path | Prerendered file | |---|---| | / | dist/index.html | | /services | dist/services/index.html | | /systems | dist/systems/index.html | | /training | dist/training/index.html | | /engagements | dist/engagements/index.html | | /about | dist/about/index.html | | /contact | dist/contact/index.html | | any unknown address | dist/404.html (status 404, "Page not found") | `sitemap.xml` lists the seven pages at https://thebayesgroup.com. `robots.txt`, `favicon.svg` and `dist/images/` (the site's photos) are copied from `public/`. **Page metadata.** Each page has one title, a description, og:title, og:description, og:url, og:type, a canonical link and the favicon. | Path | Title | Description | |---|---|---| | / | The Bayes Group \| Evidence-driven AI | Evidence-driven AI consulting, training and custom development led by two credentialed data scientists. | | /services | Services \| The Bayes Group | (as now) | | /systems | Systems engineering \| The Bayes Group | Agentic and multi-system AI, designed to be observable from day one and built to be sustained by your team. | | /training | Training \| The Bayes Group | (as now) | | /engagements | Engagements \| The Bayes Group | Right-sized AI engagements for small and medium-sized businesses, and a premium enterprise tier. | | /about, /contact, 404 | (as now) | (as now) | **Navigation states (as now)** - First load: no scroll and no focus change. - Route change: scroll to (0,0) and focus `
`. - Route change with a hash: scroll to the target with `scroll-margin-top: 96px`. - Header: when `scrollY > 0`, `.is-scrolled` adds a white background and a 1px `#E3E8EF` bottom border. **Home (in order, background in brackets)** 1. Hero [photo + navy overlay] 2. Credibility strip [white bar, overlapping the hero by 48px] 3. Who we serve [white] 4. Systems band [navy] 5. Pillars [pale] 6. How we work [white] 7. Example engagements [pale] 8. Testimonial [navy] 9. Why The Bayes Group [white] 10. CTA band [navy-deep + bell-curve motif] The last heading in main is the CTA h2. The last link in main is **Book a consultation**. **Systems** 1. Navy hero: text (eyebrow, h1, lead) and the architecture diagram. They sit side by side on desktop and stack text-then-diagram on phones and tablets. 2. `#agentic` [white] 3. `#architecture` [pale] 4. `#observability` [white] 5. `#sustainability` [pale] 6. Deliverables [navy] 7. CTA "Have a system in mind?" [pale] **Engagements** - Header [white]: h1 and intro. - Tiers [pale]: three business cards, then the full-width Enterprise card `#enterprise`. - A "Not sure which fits?" line [white]. **Services** - Navy page header band with the data-grid motif. - Three sections [white, pale, white], each with a two-column header and a grid of item cards. **Training:** photo banner, then filter and grid. - Default count: "Showing 6 courses". - Filtered count, for example: "Showing 2 courses for Managers". - Empty: "No courses for this audience yet." with **Show all courses**. **About:** mission beside the photo, two founder cards and four value cards. Each founder card has: - an amber **Placeholder** tag; - an avatar marked "Photo placeholder"; - the note "Placeholder: replace with founder credentials and bio." **Contact (in order)** 1. Navy page header band [navy + data-grid motif]: eyebrow "CONTACT", h1 "Book a consultation", the lead and the "Prefer email?" mailto line. No form in the band. 2. Form section [page's normal background, usual section padding]: the two-column form and the "What happens next" card, unchanged. Form states: - Default: empty fields, with the "Required" tag on Name, Email and Message. - Error: shown on blur and on submit; focus moves to the first invalid field. Messages: "Please enter your name." / "Please enter a valid email address." / "Please enter a message." - Success: green status banner, focused, form cleared. - Loading: none. The button is never disabled. - Company size never errors. **Not found:** bell-curve illustration, h1 "Page not found", "The page you're looking for doesn't exist or has moved.", **Back to home** and **View services**. ## Layout **Global** - Container max-width 1200px, centered. Side padding 24px (phone) / 40px (≥1024px). - `html, body { overflow-x:hidden }`. All SVG and img: `max-width:100%; height:auto`. - Breakpoints: <768 phone, 768–1023 tablet, ≥1024 desktop. - Section padding 64px (phone) / 96px (desktop). Eyebrow 12px above the h2; h2 16px above the intro; 48px from the intro to the content. **Phone (390px)** - Single column throughout. - Hero: min-height 560px; text bottom-aligned; buttons full-width and stacked, with a 12px gap. - Credibility strip: a 2×2 grid inside a white card, margin-top −48px. - Who we serve: panels stacked, SMB first. - Systems band: diagram on top (the stacked variant), capabilities below. - Systems hero: `.systems-hero__grid` is one column with a 32px gap: text first, diagram below (phone svg). - How we work: steps stacked, no connecting line. - Two-column blocks stack photo-first. - Contact: navy header band, then the form, then the "What happens next" photo card. - Footer: the three groups stack (brand, Services, Company) with a 32px gap, then the hairline and copyright. **Desktop (1280–1440px):** 12-column grid with 32px gutters. - Hero: min-height 680px. Text spans columns 1–7. The overlay is a left→right gradient. - Credibility strip: 4 columns in one bar, 24px padding. - Who we serve: SMB panel 7 columns, Enterprise panel 5 columns, equal height. - Systems band: diagram 7 columns; capabilities 5 columns, stacked as 4 rows. - Systems hero (≥1024px): `.systems-hero__grid { grid-template-columns: minmax(0,2fr) minmax(0,3fr); align-items:center; gap:48px }`. Text column (eyebrow, h1, lead) on the left, about 40%; diagram on the right, vertically centered. The base rule has no multi-column template. - Pillars: 3 columns. Examples: 3 columns. - Steps: a 4-column `ol`. A 2px `#1F8A8A` line runs behind the 48px circles at `top:24px; left:12.5%; right:12.5%`. "Operate & improve" sits below as a full-width card, 32px margin-top. - Why: photo 5 columns; a 2×2 points grid in 7 columns. - Systems sections: text 7 columns, illustration 5 columns (sides alternate). Deliverables: 3×2 grid. - Engagements: business tiers in 3 columns. Enterprise is full width as 2 columns (photo 5 | content 7). - Services headers: photo 5 columns | text 7 columns. Items: a 2-column grid. - Page header bands (Services, Systems-style inner pages, Training, Engagements, About, Contact): text block max-width 760px, left-aligned in the container. - Contact: form 7 columns | aside 5 columns, in the section below the band. - Footer (≥1024px): `.footer-grid { grid-template-columns: 2fr 1fr 1fr; gap:48px }` (brand | Services | Company), with the copyright row below a hairline. No 4-track footer rule exists. **No empty half-columns:** every text column beside a photo holds an eyebrow, an h2, a paragraph and a list, link or meta line, vertically centered. ## Design tokens **Approach:** plain CSS. The provided commit likely changed DEPLOYMENT.md accordingly. Let's examine current DEPLOYMENT.md content. It already contains sections: "Static deployment" with bullet list of eight files, includes dist/index.html (/), dist/services/index.html, dist/systems/index.html, dist/training/index.html, dist/engagements/index.html, dist/about/index.html, dist/contact/index.html, dist/404.html. The file content currently includes "dist/index.html (/)" sort of formatting inside bullet list. Let's check given content: 

```
## Static deployment
`npm run build` runs `vite build`, bundles the server renderer and then prerenders one HTML file per page into `dist/`:

- `dist/index.html` (/)
- `dist/services/index.html`
- `dist/systems/index.html`
- `dist/training/index.html`
- `dist/engagements/index.html`
- `dist/about/index.html`
- `dist/contact/index.html`
- `dist/404.html`

Upload the `dist/` folder as it is to any static host. There is no backend.
...
```

So the bullet for dist/index.html includes (/). That's correct for requirement R3: The "Static deployment" section's list of prerendered files names dist/index.html as the file for /. R3 likely requires the bullet to be `dist/index.html` (/). However, unclear if they want ``dist/index.html` (/). So maybe the bullet uses backticks around dist/index.html, then parentheses around /. Actually in the file, selection: `dist/index.html` (/). That's matched by regex used in tests. In test file deployment-doc-pages.test.ts they search bullet with pattern: they get the section text and then test if the string matches a regex:

```
test('dist/index.html is marked as the / page', () => {
   const s = section('Static deployment');
   expect(s).toMatch(/dist\/index\.html`?\s*\(\s*\/\s*\)/);
});
```

They allow optional backtick after .html. The current text is `dist/index.html` (/). That's backticks around whole `dist/index.html`. The regex: /dist\/index\.html`?\s*\(\s*\/\s*\)/ expects `dist/index.html` (maybe without backticks). In ours we have backticks around dist/index.html, like "`dist/index.html` (/)" => that matches? The regex sees "dist/index.html`" optional backtick after .html. Let's parse: The string is `dist/index.html` then space then (/). How does regex handle backticks? The pattern is `dist\/index\.html` - note a literal backtick is after .html? The pattern ends with .html; then optional `` `?` `` (a backtick). The actual string after .html has backtick, so optional will match. Then `\s*\(\s*\/\s*\)` matches after handling backticks.

Thus current bullet satisfies test.

```
## SEO files
`dist/` also contains `robots.txt` (allows everything and points to the sitemap), `sitemap.xml` (lists the seven pages at https://thebayesgroup.com: `/`, `/services`, `/systems`, `/training`, `/engagements`, `/about`, `/contact`), `favicon.svg` (linked from every page), and `dist/images/` (holds the site's photos). All of these are copied from `public/`.

In acceptance test "deployment-doc-build-match.test.ts", there are two tests: first checks that build writes dist/systems/index.html and dist/engagements/index.html (which is true). Second test ensures that the HTML files named under Static deployment are exactly the HTML files the build writes. They compare `documented = Array.from(new Set(s.match(/dist\\/[\\w./-]*?\\.html/g) || [])).sort()` to `builtHtml`, which they sort built file list from build output.

message.content:
All five fixes are in, on the contact form only. All 359 acceptance tests and every blocking validator pass. I haven't looked at fresh screenshots, so the visual result is unchecked.

- **U1, focus under the sticky header:** `.field` wrappers and `.form-control` inputs now have `scroll-margin-top: 96px`. The "Please fix…" links focus their input with `preventScroll` and then scroll the whole field into view.
- **U2, selects:** both selects use `appearance: none` and `padding-right: 48px`. They have a 20px muted chevron 16px from the right edge, and keep the same height, radius and border as the text inputs.
- **U3, error summary:** a failed submit now shows a banner above the first field and moves focus to it, not to the Name input. It reads "Please fix N fields:" followed by links to each invalid field. The brief named `errorContainer`/`onErrorContainer` tokens, which this app doesn't have, so I used hard-coded colours (`#FDECEA` background, `#7A1A12` text). It has 16px padding, an 8px radius and a 24px bottom margin.
- **U4, aside:** from 1024px up, `.contact-aside` is `position: sticky` with `top: 96px` and `align-self: start`. The phone layout stays stacked.
- **U5, "Required" badge:** the outlined pill is now plain "(required)" text with an 8px left margin, no border, in the small muted style. The existing test accepts this wording.

The changes are in `src/pages/ContactPage.tsx` and `src/styles/global.css`.

The summary shows only after a failed submit, and its links disappear as each error clears.

message.content:
On the contact form, a failed submit now shows the first invalid field (Name) in full instead of leaving it under the sticky header. All 359 acceptance tests pass, and `validate` passes. I haven't looked at a new screenshot of the errors screen.

- **Scroll and focus (`src/pages/ContactPage.tsx`):** on a failed submit, focus goes to the first invalid field with `preventScroll`. The field's wrapper (label plus input) is then scrolled into view. Before, the error summary was focused and scrolled instead.
- **Fallback:** if no invalid field is found, it still focuses and scrolls to the error summary.
- **Scroll margin (`src/styles/global.css`):** the wrapper, all inputs, selects, textareas and the error summary now have `scroll-margin-top: calc(var(--header-h) + 24px)`. That is 96px on phone and desktop. It was a hard-coded 96px on the wrapper and inputs, and the selects, textareas and error summary had none.

The focus now lands on the field, not the "Please fix N fields" summary, so a screen-reader user no longer gets that summary's alert announcement on submit.

I changed only the contact page and its styles.

After "Send message" with invalid fields, the first invalid field now scrolls into view below the sticky header, with its label visible. I didn't check this on a screenshot. The tests (359) and the `validate` run passed, but only the tests were re-run after the CSS edit. `validate` ran before it, and I never looked at a rendered result.

- **Scroll fix (`ContactPage.tsx`):** I added a small helper, `scrollBelowHeader`, that scrolls the field's wrapper (label and input), not the bare input. It leaves 96px at the top (the 72px header plus 24px). The submit handler and the error-summary links both use it. Focus still uses `preventScroll`, so the browser doesn't also jump to the bare input.
- **Scroll margin (`global.css`):** `scroll-margin-top: calc(var(--header-h) + 24px)` now also applies to inputs, selects and textareas on the contact page. The `.field` wrapper already inherited the same margin from an existing rule, which is why I didn't add it there.

I changed no logic, stores or tests. The helper catches the error jsdom throws for scrolling.

I made two changes for U1, the contact form with errors. I haven't seen a new screenshot, so I can't say the focused field is now fully visible. All 359 acceptance tests pass, and `validate` is clean apart from two non-blocking medium react-router advisories with no fix available.

- **`src/styles/global.css`:** I added `html { scroll-padding-top: calc(var(--header-h) + 24px) }`, which is 96px. Any scroll the browser starts for focus or anchors now stops below the sticky header on phone and desktop.
- **`src/pages/ContactPage.tsx`:** After Send message, the page now re-aligns the first invalid field's wrapper (label plus input) below the header at two later points, 150ms and 400ms. I did this because the error messages and summary may still be laying out when the first scroll runs.

The wrapper and input `scroll-margin-top` values and the `focus({ preventScroll: true })` call were already in place, so I left them alone. I changed nothing else.
